cleanIntro: A double-stack 1911 that strips like no other 1911: the guide rod is unscrewed half a turn BEFORE the slide stop comes out, and the recoil system leaves through the front of the slide rather than the back. Springfield publishes two versions of the front end and the one you have decides which half you follow.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger off, magazine out
steps.action: Point it somewhere harmless with your finger outside the guard, then drop the magazine. A 1911 DS fires with the magazine out if a round is chambered — the book prints that in capitals for a reason.
steps.aside: ALWAYS REMEMBER THE FIREARM IS ABLE TO FIRE WITH OR WITHOUT THE MAGAZINE IN PLACE.
steps.quote: POINT GUN IN SAFE DIRECTION WHILE KEEPING FINGER OFF THE TRIGGER.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.22, per Figures 22-1 and 22-2 on the page)

steps.title: Slide locked back, chamber proved empty, glasses on
steps.action: Retract the slide and lift the slide stop into the slide-stop notch to lock it open, then look into the chamber and put a finger in. Eye protection goes on now: everything after this is under spring tension.
steps.quote: Unload the pistol and lock the slide to the rear by retracting the slide and lifting the slide stop lever up into the slide stop notch in the slide (Figure 22-1).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.22, per Figures 22-1 and 22-2 on the page)

steps.title: Guide rod loosened HALF a turn — and no further
steps.action: With the slide still locked back, put a 5/32 hex wrench on the guide rod and turn it half a turn counterclockwise. Half a turn: unscrewing it fully at this point releases the recoil spring while the slide is still under tension, which is the opposite of what you want.
steps.aside: NOTE: The slide is under spring tension so maintain control for the following steps.
steps.quote: With the slide locked to the rear and using a 5/32 hex wrench, loosen the guide rod ½ turn counterclockwise but do not completely unscrew the rod.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.22, per Figures 22-1 and 22-2 on the page)

steps.title: Disassembly notch aligned, slide stop out right to left
steps.action: Line the disassembly notch in the slide up with the slide stop and push the stop out from right to left. Keep a hand on the slide as it comes free — the spring is still doing work.
steps.quote: Align the disassembly notch in the slide with the slide stop and remove the slide stop from the pistol in a right to left motion (Figure 22-2).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.22, per Figures 22-1 and 22-2 on the page)

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame rails, under control
steps.action: Hold the slide and run it forward off the frame rails. Control it all the way — this is a full-length guide rod gun and the tension does not end where a GI 1911's does.
steps.quote: While maintaining control of the slide remove the slide assembly from the frame by moving the slide forward and off the frame rails (Figure 23-1).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.23-24, per Figures 23-1, 23-2 and 24-1)

steps.title: Guide rod section out of the front, then the head and spring
steps.action: Finish unscrewing the guide rod section and take it out of the front of the slide, then lift the guide rod head and recoil spring out — the head is under spring tension until it clears. Keep the parts in order; the reverse spring plug behind them comes next.
steps.aside: Carefully as the guide rod head is under spring tension, lift and remove the guide rod head and recoil spring from the slide and spring plug (Figure 24-1).
steps.quote: Unscrew the guide rod section and remove from front of slide (Figure 23-2).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.23-24, per Figures 23-1, 23-2 and 24-1)

steps.title: Reverse spring plug rearward out of its tunnel
steps.action: Slide the reverse spring plug rearward out of the recoil spring tunnel in the slide. It only travels one way, and forcing it forward mars the tunnel.
steps.quote: Remove the reverse spring plug from its home by sliding it rearward from the recoil spring tunnel in the slide.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.23-24, per Figures 23-1, 23-2 and 24-1)

steps.title: Barrel lifted 1/8" at the lug, then straight out the front
steps.action: Grasp the barrel lug, lift about an eighth of an inch, and draw the barrel forward out of the slide while keeping the lug vertical. Let the lug rotate and it will catch; that is the whole trick of a bull-barrel 1911 DS.
steps.quote: Grasp the barrel lug and lift upwards 1/8” and then slide the barrel forward and out of the slide while maintaining vertical orientation of the barrel lug (Figure 24-2). Field stripping is now complete.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP (printed p.23-24, per Figures 23-1, 23-2 and 24-1)

steps.title: If yours is a DUAL RECOIL SPRING gun, this is your front end instead
steps.action: A 1911 DS built with a dual recoil spring system does not use the hex wrench at all: lock the slide back, take the slide stop out, ease the slide off, then with the slide upside down press the guide rod head forward and snap the takedown piece over the exposed rod before the spring system will come out. Barrel out of the front last, as before.
steps.aside: The recoil spring system can now be removed from the slide (Figure 24-4).
steps.quote: With the bottom of the slide facing up, press the guide rod head forward until enough of the rod is exposed and firmly snap the takedown piece over the rod (Figure 24-3).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — FIELD STRIP — dual recoil spring variant (printed p.24, per Figure 24-3)

steps.title: Bore from the chamber end, brush then patches
steps.action: Rod in from the chamber end where possible, solvent-wet patch through several times, then the bristle brush end to end, then dry patches until they come out clean. Never reverse a brush inside the bore.
steps.aside: Do not “reverse” rod direction when patch or brush is in barrel, it might bind.
steps.quote: Using cleaning rod, run solvent-wetted patch through barrel several times.
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING FIREARM (printed p.53, per Figures 53-1 to 53-3)

steps.title: One drop per slide way — then work it in
steps.action: Springfield is specific about lubrication on this pistol: one drop of oil to each slide way, slide fitted bare and worked back and forth to spread it, then one drop at the chamber area and one just behind the muzzle once assembled. That is the whole oiling schedule — more than that collects dust.
steps.aside: DO NOT APPLY EXCESS LUBRICATING OIL.
steps.quote: Apply one drop of oil to each of the slide ways (Figure 53-1).
steps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — CLEANING FIREARM (printed p.53, per Figures 53-1 to 53-3)

deepSteps.title: Magazine base off — the locking plate is behind the base
deepSteps.action: Look through the bottom of the magazine base for the exposed protrusion of the locking plate, press it in, and slide the base forward while you hold it. A double-stack 1911 magazine has real spring load behind that base and it will launch the follower if you let go.
deepSteps.aside: NOTE: There is considerable spring pressure bearing on the magazine base.
deepSteps.quote: Disassembly of the 1911 DS magazine is accomplished by depressing the exposed protrusion of the magazine locking plate that is visible through the bottom surface of the magazine base (Figure 30-1).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING PROCEDURES FOR THE 1911 DS 9MM MAGAZINES (printed p.30, per Figure 30-1 on the page)

deepSteps.title: Spring controlled out, and note which way round it goes
deepSteps.action: Ease the spring out under control and lay it down the way it came — the book asks you to note its orientation because a magazine spring fitted upside down feeds badly and looks perfectly normal. Clean the body and follower dry; oil inside a magazine collects grit and reaches the ammunition.
deepSteps.aside: NOTE: MAKE NOTE OF MAGAZINE SPRING ORIENTATION.
deepSteps.quote: Control the magazine spring as the base is removed (Figure 30-3).
deepSteps.cite: Springfield Armory 1911 DS Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, current support-site edition (no part code printed). ⛔ No page folios are printed; printed pages are read off the figure captions on the same page. — DISASSEMBLY AND CLEANING PROCEDURES FOR THE 1911 DS 9MM MAGAZINES (printed p.30, per Figure 30-1 on the page)

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Solvent-wet patch, bristle brush end to end, dry patches until clean
Residue in the chamber interferes with feeding — clean it, not just the bore
Dry patch, then one lightly oiled patch

cleaning.name: SLIDE & BREECH
tasks: Solvent and a bristle brush on the breech face, extractor and feed ramp
Wipe the recoil spring tunnel and the guide rod parts
⛔ No oil or grease on the striker

cleaning.name: FRAME & RAILS
tasks: Powder residue off with solvent on a patch, then wipe dry
One drop of oil per slide way, worked in with the bare slide

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Strip and clean per the deep-clean steps; body and follower dry
Check the feed lips for nicks and deformation before reloading them

reassembly: Barrel into the front of the slide, lug vertical, seated down into its cut.
Reverse spring plug back into the recoil spring tunnel from the rear.
Guide rod head and recoil spring into the slide against the plug, then the front guide rod section threaded in from the front — finger tight for now.
Slide onto the frame rails and drawn back to line the disassembly notch up with the slide stop hole.
Slide stop in from the left, then lock the slide back and tighten the guide rod with the 5/32 hex wrench.
Dual-recoil-spring guns: recoil system into the slide with the takedown piece still fitted, slide onto the frame, slide stop in, then remove the takedown piece last.
Function test before any live ammunition.
fncheck: Reassemble, magazine out, chamber empty, muzzle safe. Cycle the slide by hand several times — it should run without binding and lock back on an empty magazine. Check the thumb safety only engages with the hammer cocked and that it blocks the trigger, and that the grip safety releases the trigger only when depressed. If anything is inconsistent, stop and call Springfield or a gunsmith rather than firing it.
